basics.name: Ernest Moyo
basics.label: Epidemiologist and Health Data Scientist | Bayesian malaria mapping and AI for health in Africa
basics.summary: Epidemiologist and health data scientist with 15 years in data and analytics, nine of them in public health with ministries of health across Southern and East Africa. PhD researcher with the Vector Atlas (University of Oxford, icipe and The Kids Research Institute Australia), registered at NM-AIST; Research Scientist with the Malaria Atlas Project (East Africa node, Ifakara Health Institute); Co-Founder of 7Square Inc. (founded 2021) and of Hoop Africa Foundation. Trains national malaria programme teams in geospatial modelling and builds analytics capacity in the institutions that use the models. Trained as an actuary.

work.name: Vector Atlas (University of Oxford, icipe and The Kids Research Institute Australia)
work.summary: Doctoral research with the Vector Atlas, an initiative of the University of Oxford, the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe) and The Kids Research Institute Australia, working alongside the Malaria Atlas Project and funded by the Gates Foundation. Registered for the PhD at the Nelson Mandela African Institution of Science and Technology (NM-AIST). Supervised by Prof. Nick Golding.

work.name: Malaria Atlas Project, East Africa node (Ifakara Health Institute)
work.summary: Scientific and technical support to the MAP East Africa node, working with the Malaria Atlas Project teams in Perth and Dar es Salaam and with the Vector Atlas to plan analytic support for national malaria programmes. Builds Bayesian and machine-learning models (Gaussian-process, geostatistical, spatio-temporal) that combine household surveys, DHIS2 routine data, entomological and satellite data into malaria risk maps.
highlights: Capacity building and modelling literacy: builds learning tracks and trains national malaria programme staff to interpret, question and apply model outputs, including geospatial modelling workshops in Nairobi for Kenya (April 2026, MaMOD Africa) and in Maputo for Mozambique with CISM (September 2026); key faculty in the MAP early-career researcher programme.

Surveillance and risk stratification: workflows that carry geospatial outputs into stratification, Global Fund applications, programme reviews and national surveillance guidelines, including risk validation and stratification with Namibia (2026).

Risk mapping with national malaria programmes and CHAI for national strategic plans, from DHIS2 routine data, facility geocoding and data-quality review, with accessibility maps and community health worker allocation analysis.
Stakeholder engagement: translates MAP methods and outputs for ministries of health and partners (WHO, CHAI, PATH), and proactively brings modelling products to programmes where they add value.
Model enhancement: brings vector data into malaria risk mapping (PhD focus) and prepares analysable datasets from surveillance reports, surveys and environmental covariates.

work.name: 7Square Inc.
work.summary: Data, AI and engineering company converting Africa's challenges into opportunities. Works with governments, health programmes, regulators and industry to turn hard problems into systems that work, and leaves the skills behind with the people who run them.
highlights: Malaria risk maps that update as new data arrives, so nets and medicines go where they are needed.
Regional disaster-response, port operations, conservation-alert and private in-country AI systems.
Working in 12 countries across Southern and East Africa.

work.name: FABRIC (Fungal burden, risk and the impacts of climate), University of Oxford, Nuffield Department of Medicine, funded by Wellcome
work.summary: FABRIC is building the global evidence base on where the most important human fungal pathogens are and how a changing climate may affect them. Contributes the systematic literature reviews on climate and fungal burden and on the reported distribution of fungal pathogens: inclusion criteria, search strategy and screening.

highlights: 2026: facilitation team for an AI programme for young entrepreneurs at the Gordon Institute of Business Science (GIBS), South Africa.

work.position: Consultant (Tanzania Country Lead; Digital Systems Support)
work.summary: Consultant to Market Access Africa on successive assignments in malaria treatment, access to health products and regional pooled procurement.
highlights: Tanzania Country Lead on multi-country stakeholder research on malaria treatment (2025 to 2026).
Qualitative interview analysis, including AI-assisted transcription and coding.
Digital systems support to regional pooled procurement work (2026).
Market research support (2022).

work.name: NTD Modelling Consortium (University of Oxford, Gates Foundation)
work.position: Senior Research and Data Scientist (PAMCA) and Research Scientist (Ifakara Health Institute)
work.summary: Joined through the Gates Foundation-funded NTD Modelling Consortium grant, led by the University of Oxford Big Data Institute, in which the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association (PAMCA) builds neglected tropical disease modelling capacity in Africa with Ifakara Health Institute as its centre of excellence. Senior Research and Data Scientist with PAMCA from February 2024, then Research Scientist (collaborator) at Ifakara Health Institute on the DM4DM project from July 2024. Built predictive models for malaria and NTD elimination and supported national programmes to use them.
highlights: Seconded to the Center for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (CEMA), University of Nairobi, to continue the NTD Modelling Consortium work until July 2025.
Supported the build of MosquitoDB, a vector-surveillance database, and its web decision-support tools.

work.name: Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI)
work.summary: Staff epidemiologist from July 2021 to March 2024, then consultant to December 2025.
highlights: Led malaria risk stratification and transmission-driver analyses in Angola, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and South Africa, with the Malaria Atlas Project and Swiss TPH.
Designed national malaria data-use strategies for Namibia and Zimbabwe, and designed and piloted focus investigations in Namibia.
Led malaria programme reviews in Namibia and Zimbabwe; supported Global Fund funding requests for Zimbabwe, Namibia and Angola.

work.name: Delta Philanthropies and Higherlife Foundation
work.position: Head of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation
work.summary: Ran monitoring and evaluation across Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Kenya and Burundi for rural transformation, education, WASH, nutrition, public health and disaster-relief programmes.
highlights: Monitoring and evaluation lead for the Cholera Elimination Secretariat, hosted by Higherlife Foundation and funded by Delta Philanthropies: updated the cholera M&E frameworks, Theories of Change, targets and indicators.
Contributed to Zimbabwe's cholera elimination operational plan and hotspot prioritisation with the Ministry of Health and Child Care and WHO (2020-2021).
Designed the cholera knowledge, attitudes and practices study tools and built KoBoToolbox and ODK data collection tools for cholera, education and agriculture programmes.
Led the UNICEF Spotlight Initiative baseline on violence against women and girls in Zimbabwe (2019-2020).
Managed 8 to 12 staff across four countries.

work.name: World Health Organization (Zimbabwe) and Ministry of Health and Child Care, Zimbabwe
work.summary: Analysed and wrote up the investigation of a COVID-19 outbreak in a closed population (John Tallach High School, Umguza District, Matabeleland North).
highlights: Extracted field data, reconciled the outbreak line list across testing cycles and produced the epidemic curve.
Authored the outbreak investigation report through review rounds with WHO and Ministry of Health and Child Care surveillance and emergency preparedness teams.

work.name: Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), with the Ministry of Health and Child Care, Zimbabwe
highlights: Led Zimbabwe's first national rollout of DHIS2 Tracker for malaria case and focus investigation.
Developed surveillance indicators and mapping guidelines; the focus-investigation guidelines were later adopted by other countries.
Trained health staff from provincial to ward level.
Cross-border malaria collaboration with Botswana.
